name: Pegvisomant
route: Daily injection under the skin after a supervised loading dose
status: FDA-approved (2003) for acromegaly not controlled by surgery or radiation
mechanism: Modified growth hormone that occupies the growth hormone receptor without switching it on, so the liver makes far less IGF-1

article.summary: Pegvisomant (Somavert) is a daily injection for acromegaly that blocks the growth hormone receptor, normalizing IGF-1 in most patients when surgery or radiation has not worked.
article.takeaway: Acromegaly is caused by a pituitary tumor that makes too much growth hormone, which raises IGF-1 and enlarges hands, feet, face and organs. Pegvisomant takes a different approach from other drugs: rather than reducing growth hormone, it **blocks the receptor** that growth hormone acts on.[^1] In early trials IGF-1 became normal in up to 89% of patients on the highest dose, and in 97% of those treated for a year or more.[^2][^3] Real-world rates are lower but still substantial, and liver tests and tumor size need monitoring.[^4]
glance: Acromegaly with an inadequate response to surgery or radiation, or when those are not appropriate
40 mg loading dose, then a daily injection under the skin adjusted by IGF-1 levels
Randomized trial, long-term studies and a 2,221-patient real-world registry

blocks.text: Growth hormone switches on its receptor by binding two receptor units at once. Pegvisomant is growth hormone with several amino acid changes: it still binds the receptor tightly but cannot trigger the shape change that sends the signal. Polyethylene glycol (PEG) chains attached to it slow its clearance.

The result is a steep fall in IGF-1, the hormone behind most acromegaly symptoms. Growth hormone levels in the blood actually rise during treatment, and pegvisomant also interferes with standard growth hormone tests, so doctors track IGF-1 instead.[^1]

Somavert is approved for acromegaly in people whose disease is not controlled after surgery or radiation, or for whom those treatments are not appropriate. The goal is a normal IGF-1 level.[^1] It is often used when somatostatin analogs such as [octreotide](/peptides/octreotide) or [lanreotide](/peptides/lanreotide) are not enough, and sometimes in combination with them.

rows: Normal IGF-1 in 54%, 81% and 89% on 10, 15 and 20 mg daily vs 10% on placebo[^2]
152 patients on daily injections for up to 18 months
97% of those treated for 12 months or more reached normal IGF-1[^3]
Normal IGF-1 in 54% at one year and 75% at ten years[^4]

blocks.text: Registry control rates climbed over the years as more patients moved to higher doses.[^4] In the randomized trial, ring size, soft-tissue swelling, sweating and fatigue also improved.[^2]

Treatment begins with a 40 mg loading dose given under medical supervision, followed by 10 mg injected under the skin each day. The dose is adjusted in 5 mg steps every 4-6 weeks based on IGF-1, usually within 10-30 mg a day, with 30 mg as the label maximum.[^1]

items: **Common:** infections, pain, nausea, diarrhea, flu-like symptoms and injection-site reactions
**Liver:** raised liver enzymes; tests are checked before and during treatment[^1]
**Low blood sugar** in people with diabetes, because insulin sensitivity improves; diabetes drugs may need lowering
**Fat changes under the skin** where injections are repeated; rotate sites
**Tumor growth:** the drug does not act on the tumor, so pituitary MRI scans continue

blocks.text: In the ACROSTUDY registry, tumor enlargement was seen on imaging in 7.1% of patients and abnormal liver tests in 3.2%; side effects led to stopping the drug in 1.3%.[^4]

evidence.label: Strong: effective IGF-1 control over two decades
evidence.text: A randomized placebo-controlled trial and long-term follow-up show that pegvisomant lowers IGF-1 in a dose-dependent way.[^2][^3] A large registry spanning more than a decade confirms durable control and a manageable safety profile.[^4]

faq.q: Does pegvisomant shrink the pituitary tumor?
faq.a: No. It blocks growth hormone's effects but does not act on the tumor, so regular MRI scans are part of treatment. Most tumors stay stable.[^4]

faq.q: Why is growth hormone not used to check whether it works?
faq.a: Growth hormone levels rise on treatment and the drug interferes with growth hormone tests. IGF-1 is the marker used to adjust the dose.[^1]

faq.q: Can it be combined with other acromegaly drugs?
faq.a: Yes. Combining it with somatostatin analogs became increasingly common in real-world practice, although that goes beyond the label.[^5] The choice is made by the treating endocrinologist.
